Khanam Matra Sarest is the Khanam Matra of the Maruuk centaur of the Ohn'ahran Plains. As such, she is the leader of Clan Teerai, the cultural khan of all the Maruuk clans, and a direct descendant of Teera herself. She rules from atop the krutal in Maruukai and is protected by the khansguard.

meeting with Gemisath and khans Tigari and Sansok during the Khural.]] The Khural is a gathering of the Maruuk centaur clans held each season at Maruukai, in the center of the Ohn'ahran Plains. It is a time of truce and discussion, when clans large and small come together from across the plains to share resources and stories. The event is organized and overseen by Clan Teerai, the Maruuk's tradition keepers. Many centaur take the opportunity to reconnect with clanmates and family members. The gathering lasts many days, and it is "almost impossible" to coordinate all of the logistics. Providing food for all of the attending centaur is especially challenging. .]] Khanam Matra (also written khanam matra, sometimes just khanam) is the title given to the leader of Clan Teerai, who acts as the cultural khan of all Maruuk centaur. All Khanam Matras can trace their bloodlines back to the Maruuk's first matriarch, Teera. The daughters of a Khanam Matra are given the special title or surname Dotur, and they dedicate their lives to upholding traditions and serving the Maruuk in many ways. When a Khanam Matra dies, a new one is chosen from her daughters and granddaughters, ensuring the continuation of Teera's bloodline. The Khanam Matra is protected by the khansguard. The current holder of the title is Khanam Matra Sarest.
The Khanam Matra's Message is provided by Khanam Matra Sarest for Hooves of War to be delivered to Khansguard Jebotai.

After Clan Nokhud declare war on the other clans, the Khanam Matra orders Jebotai to rally the Teerai's forces, prepare Teerakai's defenses, and inform Clan Ohn'ir that they need to contact Ohn'ahra. After adventurers bring Jebotai's orders to the townsfolk of Teerakai, he sends them on to Initiate Boku to commune with Ohn'ahra. Kirtonos the Herald is an undead who can transform into a vampire. Long ago, he became the master of Scholomance's Doctor Theolen Krastinov. Responsible for many of the atrocities during Krastinov's rule over Scholomance, Kirtonos fed on the blood of his innocent victims. To appease his master, Doctor Krastinov had to provide the gargoyle with more and more blood. In later days, Kirtonos was a rare visitor to Scholomance. The Blood of Innocents was not easy to obtain around Caer Darrow now that most of its inhabitants were dead. Only the ghosts remained, plotting the vampire's demise.

King Gordok, formerly known as Ulrok, is an ogre in Dire Maul North. The title of the king of the Gordunni ogres, residing inside Dire Maul. To become king, you'll have to kill the king that's ruling over the ogres at that point, whoever it is. The Gordoks will respect you through that, and will shower you with gifts. The only disadvantage of being King Gordok is that you can never leave Dire Maul — the ogres will appoint another when you stroll away. Terrible whispers from the Emerald Nightmare plagued King Gordok's mind, urging him to madness and slaughter. He commanded his clan to indiscriminately murder anyone they could find. __NOTOC__ Kinelory (or Kin) is a night elf quest giver located at Go'Shek Farm in the Arathi Highlands. She is a scout working under Phin Odelic to investigate rumors of a new plague created by the Forsaken at Go'Shek Farm. After investigating, she and Quae broke up a plot to create a new plague in Arathi. During the Cataclysm, Kinelory and Quae, now working for Commander Amaren, team up again to undermine the Forsaken's efforts to expand into the Arathi Highlands. She's very close to Quae, who calls her "Kin" and is very protective about her. Apparently, Kinelory sometimes gets in a fight in taverns.

.]] King Ymiron was the king of the vrykul in Northrend. His people, the Dragonflayer clan, are still fanatically loyal to him. Having proven himself to the Lich King, he was converted to the undead and is the last boss of Utgarde Pinnacle. When defeated by adventurers, Ymiron found the Halls of Valor closed to him for his betrayal against Odyn. Helya brought him into her service in the Maw of Souls instead. As Helheim was stormed by order champions, the Battlelord of the Valarjar convinced Odyn to raise the Fallen King so he could be forced to serve the Keeper for eternity, a fitting punishment for dooming his own people.

King's Harbor is located to the southeast of New Avalon, below the Scarlet Overlook on the bluffs. Its docks are initially controlled by the Scarlet Crusade, but later by the Knights of the Ebon Blade after the fall of New Avalon.

King of the Fire Festival is an achievement awarded for completing the quest A Thief's Reward, which is offered once a character has completed all four "Stealing s Flame" quests. Since A Thief's Reward is immediately available to players who have completed the flame stealing quests in previous years, a player who did so before the release of Wrath of the Lich King will be able to quickly earn this achievement without re-visiting the enemy capitals. Completing this achievement is an objective of the meta achievements The Flame Keeper and The Flame Warden.

The King's Hoard is the entrance hall of Utgarde Pinnacle. As the name implies, there are heaps of gold and other treasure throughout the room - all the wealth of King Ymiron. The problem is it all happens to be cursed: Brigg Smallshanks' fellow crewmembers leaped at sight of it and paid for it with their lives, becoming undead skeletons. The locked gate at the end of the long hall leads into Ymiron's Seat, the King's throne room. The gate will only open once Ymiron is dead.
King of the Jungle is a talent in the Feral Combat tree, you will need to spend 13 points in Feral Combat to max it. It is a prerequisite for Primal Madness.

Kings' Rest is a sub-zone just west of the center of Ashran, on . Kings' Rest is a small, open area with links to nearby secondary areas Ashmaul Burial Grounds, Ring of Conquest and Amphitheater of Annihilation. The area is notable for holding the Marketplace Graveyard, a capturable graveyard and the only resurrection point outside of the faction bases. The Graveyard can be captured similarly to bases in Eye of the Storm, with the balance of players of each faction in the area determining the movement of the capture bar. __NOTOC__ King Togwaggle is the king of all kobolds on Azeroth, featured in the Kobolds & Catacombs expansion for Hearthstone. He has been described as "the big cheese, the head rat, the be-candled King of the Kobolds". He sports a crown with an actual lantern in place of the typical kobold candle, has treasure strapped to his back for safekeeping (likely obtained mostly from other kobolds), and wields a "regal shovel, lest anyone question his sovereignty". There is a secret to the lantern he wears on his head. Togwaggle is noted to be larger than his fellow kobolds (which isn't saying much) and is also rather more rotund, as there are apparently "culinary benefits" to being king.
King Needle was a podling located near some recently-formed tar pits in Gorgrond.

King Forgalash is a sea giant. In the beta version of Legion, he was the leader of the Trenchwalkers. The empty location Forgalash's Den bears his name. Dying Trenchwalker skrog will often cry , suggesting he still may be a leader within the Trenchwalkers. His current status is thus unknown. The quest King Forgalash's Burden, which did not make it out of beta, made it clear that King Forgalash conferred with Tidemistress Sashj'tar multiple times. The vrykul of Jandvik would thus send aventurers to kill him. Regardless of the omission of this questline in the game, the Trenchwalkers are still strong allies of the Sashj'tar. King Morgalash, another Trenchwalker NPC, has a very similar name and
King Dazar is the final boss of Kings' Rest. He is followed by Reban and T'zala, his raptors.
Kings' Rest Guild Run is a dungeon achievement earned for defeating Dazar in Kings' Rest while in a guild group.

Kingsmouth River is a river born in Mount Mugamba. It runs across Zuldazar, first going northeast and after splitting it goes southeast through the Garden of the Loa until reaching Dazar'alor. From there it goes south, forming a number of impressive waterfalls, and finally emptying into the South Seas in the Bay of Kings. The underwater Dive Bar is located right at its end.

Kiting is the act of running away from an enemy while staying in combat with them. It may involve staying out of melee range while delivering damage, or it can mean luring an enemy to another location on purpose. When used as a damage tactic, kiting is best suited to classes who deal most of their damage from range and are weak in melee range. Mages and ranged hunters frequently rely on it. Kiting is mostly used to allow the player to defeat the enemy without allowing them to get close enough for the player to take melee damage.
